rubrics.justification: Accurately describes a good-quality blastocyst with dense ICM, cohesive TE, substantial blastocoel, and notes the plausible 3AA vs 4AA expansion discrepancy; minor limitation is some image-based uncertainty and cautious speculation about partial collapse.
Thoroughly integrates age, embryo grade, endometrial thickness, ovarian response, AMH, BMI, semen parameters, endometriosis, and prior ectopic history into prognosis and management.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with prognosis appropriately tempered by endometriosis and ectopic/tubal concerns; only minor issue is some uncertainty around morphology while still giving a fairly confident estimate.

Recommendations are well aligned with Gardner grading principles, single embryo transfer practice in a young patient with a high-quality blastocyst, and standard attention to hydrosalpinx, luteal support, and early ectopic surveillance.

Provides clear, practical next steps including SET, luteal support adherence, serial beta-hCG, early ultrasound, tubal/hydrosalpinx review, and nuanced future planning regarding endometriosis, PGT-A, and protocol changes.
